name: HDFC Bank

icici.label: ICICI Bank FY26 results (Free Press Journal)

brief.t: India's largest private sector bank. It merged with its parent, HDFC Ltd (the home-loan company), on 1 July 2023.
New leadership: Anup Bagchi became MD & CEO on 27 Oct 2026, and Rajiv Kumar became Part-time Chairman on 15 Jul 2026.
FY 2025-26 net profit was ₹74,671 crore, up about 11% over the previous year.
Loan quality is strong: Gross NPA fell to 1.11% in Sep 2026, among the lowest in Indian banking.
Deposits grew 18.8% to about ₹33.3 lakh crore by Sep 2026, a key focus after the merger.

timeline.t: Set up as one of the first private banks after RBI opened banking to private players; promoted by HDFC Ltd.
Merged with parent HDFC Ltd, creating India's largest private bank.
Chairman Atanu Chakraborty resigned; Keki Mistry served as interim chairman.
Rajiv Kumar (former Finance Secretary and Chief Election Commissioner) became Part-time Chairman.
Anup Bagchi took charge as MD & CEO, succeeding Sashidhar Jagdishan.

model.how: A bank earns mainly by lending money at a higher rate than it pays depositors. That gap is its Net Interest Income. It also earns fees from cards, loans, and selling insurance and mutual funds.
flow: Depositors put money in (savings, current, fixed deposits)
Bank lends it out (home, personal, car, business loans)
Keeps profit after costs and provisions

points: Banks need RBI approval to appoint their chairman and CEO. That's why HDFC Bank's 2026 leadership changes waited for RBI clearance.
Private banks compete with public sector banks (like SBI) and fast-growing digital payments and fintech firms.
Big theme for interviews: banks are racing to raise deposits as loan demand grows.

people.name: Anup Bagchi
people.note: Spent over 30 years in the ICICI Group; was MD & CEO of ICICI Prudential Life before joining. Term runs to Oct 2029.

people.name: Rajiv Kumar
people.note: Former Finance Secretary and 25th Chief Election Commissioner of India. Three-year term approved by RBI.

people.name: Sashidhar Jagdishan
people.note: Led the bank through the HDFC Ltd merger.

people_changes.t: Puneet Sharma takes over as Chief Financial Officer from 1 Dec 2026.

points.t: Net profit ₹19,510 cr, up 4.7%. Lower treasury gains held back growth.
Gross NPA improved to 1.11%; Net NPA 0.37%.

numbers.say: HDFC Bank keeps about ₹20 as profit from every ₹100 it earns, and only about 1 in every 100 rupees it lends has gone bad.

rivals.note: SBI is a public sector bank. Among private banks, HDFC Bank earns the most profit.

network.local: With half its branches in semi-urban and rural areas, HDFC Bank has a large presence across Punjab and North India. Branch banking and sales roles are often posted in these towns.

employer.note: From the bank's FY 2025-26 annual report. In FY26 the bank had fewer non-supervisory staff and more managers, and invested heavily in AI training.

csr.t: HDFC Bank's CSR programme is called Parivartan. It works on rural development, education, skill training, healthcare and financial literacy.

s.t: Largest private bank; FY26 net profit ₹74,671 cr
Very clean loan book: Gross NPA 1.11%

w.t: CASA ratio of 34.1% is lower than before the merger, so deposits cost more

o.t: About half the branches are in semi-urban and rural India, where many people still lack bank loans
AI to cut costs: 50,000+ staff trained in GenAI

t.t: SBI and ICICI Bank compete hard for the same deposits and customers
Leadership changes in 2026 put governance in focus

Role knowledge, the bank and HR questions

Finance.q: What is NPA, and what is HDFC Bank's Gross NPA?
Finance.a: An NPA is a loan on which the borrower hasn't paid for 90 days. HDFC Bank's Gross NPA was 1.11% in Sep 2026, one of the lowest in India.

Finance.q: Why does CASA ratio matter to a bank?
Finance.a: CASA deposits pay little or no interest, so a higher CASA ratio means cheaper money for lending. HDFC Bank's CASA ratio was 34.1% in Mar 2026.

Finance.q: How did the HDFC Ltd merger change the bank?
Finance.a: It brought in a large home-loan book funded by borrowings, so the bank now needs to grow deposits faster. That's why deposit growth (18.8% in Sep 2026) is watched closely.

Marketing.q: How would you get more college students to open an HDFC Bank account?
Marketing.a: Use campus tie-ups, a zero-balance student account, app-first onboarding and referral rewards. Link it to a first credit card later.

Marketing.q: How is HDFC Bank's brand different from SBI's?
Marketing.a: SBI is seen as the trusted government bank with the widest reach; HDFC Bank is seen as a fast, service-focused private bank. Give one example you've experienced.

Marketing.q: Half its branches are in semi-urban and rural areas. How would you market there?
Marketing.a: Use local language, branch events, shopkeeper current accounts, and gold or tractor loans relevant to the area.

HR.q: Employee turnover is about 23%. How would you reduce it?
HR.a: Better onboarding, realistic job previews for sales roles, a buddy system, clear growth paths and early recognition. Track 90-day attrition.

HR.q: How would you hire 45,000+ people a year efficiently?
HR.a: Campus tie-ups, online assessments, standard interview scorecards and an HR tech system to track candidates.

HR.q: How do you handle an unhappy high-performing employee?
HR.a: Listen first, find the real issue (pay, manager, growth), act on what you can, and follow up.

Sales.a: Ask about the customer's needs first, then link features (app, UPI, debit card, sweep FD) to those needs. Close with a clear next step.

Sales.q: How will you handle monthly targets?
Sales.a: Break the target into daily activity, focus on existing customers for cross-sell, and track progress each week.

Operations.q: How would you cut account-opening time?
Operations.a: Digital KYC, pre-filled forms, removing duplicate checks, and tracking turnaround time at each step.

Operations.q: What is KYC and why does it matter?
Operations.a: Know Your Customer: verifying identity to prevent fraud and money laundering. It's required by RBI.

Other.q: What do you know about HDFC Bank?
Other.a: India's largest private bank. It merged with HDFC Ltd in 2023, earned ₹74,671 cr profit in FY26, and is led by MD & CEO Anup Bagchi since Oct 2026.

glossary.Net profit: What is left after all costs, provisions and taxes. The bank's final earnings.
glossary.Net profit margin: Net profit as a % of total income. 20% means ₹20 profit for every ₹100 earned.
glossary.Total income: Everything the bank earns: interest on loans plus fees and other income.
glossary.Net Interest Income: Interest earned on loans minus interest paid on deposits. A bank's main earning.
glossary.Other income: Money earned apart from interest, such as fees, commissions and trading gains.
glossary.Gross NPA: Non-Performing Asset: a loan not repaid for 90+ days. Gross NPA is the % of all loans that have gone bad.
glossary.Net NPA: Bad loans after subtracting the money already set aside (provisions) for them. Lower is better.
glossary.CASA ratio: Share of deposits in Current and Savings accounts. These pay little interest, so a higher CASA means cheaper funds.
glossary.Capital adequacy ratio: The bank's own capital compared with the risk in its loans. RBI requires a minimum; higher means safer.
glossary.Cost-to-income ratio: Operating costs as a % of income. Lower means the bank runs more efficiently.
glossary.Deposits: Money customers keep with the bank in savings, current and fixed deposit accounts.
glossary.Advances: Loans given by the bank to customers and businesses.
glossary.Dividend: Part of the profit paid to shareholders, per share.
glossary.Treasury gains: Profit from buying and selling bonds and other investments. It can swing a lot each quarter.
glossary.Attrition: The % of employees who leave in a year. Also called employee turnover.
glossary.RBI: Reserve Bank of India, which regulates all banks in India.
glossary.KYC: Know Your Customer: checking a customer's identity before opening an account.
glossary.MSME: Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises: small businesses that banks lend to.
glossary.BRSR: Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report: an official yearly report on people, environment and governance that big listed companies must publish.
glossary.Cross-sell: Selling an extra product (like a credit card) to an existing customer.
